**Last modified date:** The content I have doesn't include one. The page text is truncated before any footer or "Last modified" line, so I can't determine it from this excerpt.

**concurrencyPolicy: Forbid:** The visible text says:

> `Forbid`: The CronJob does not allow concurrent runs; if it is time for a new Job run and the previous Job run hasn't finished yet, the CronJob skips the new Job run. Also note that when the previous Job run finishes, `.spec.startingDeadlineSeconds` is still taken into account and may result in a new Job run.

It also notes that concurrency policy only applies to Jobs created by the same CronJob. Jobs from different CronJobs can always run concurrently.

**Idempotency:** The visible portion doesn't discuss idempotency in connection with `Forbid` or anywhere else. The truncated "CronJob limitations" section (including "Job creation") likely covers it, since the page's limitations section typically warns that a CronJob can occasionally create more than one Job for a single schedule time. From general Kubernetes behavior, you should design the Job's work to be idempotent, because `Forbid` prevents overlapping runs but doesn't guarantee exactly-once execution.
